In an alternative Mexico City, community gardens abound with clean air, people warmly attending workshops on sustainable water management led by hydrologists. The authoritarian state has stepped back allowing for active civic society and trusted ministries. Environmental collapse is minimal, mornings are crisp, and resilient canal systems ensure plentiful well-managed water. Social conflict is low, streets harmonious with little political tension. Capitalist hegemony supports cooperative credit among vendors at tianguis markets, fostering an environment of mutual aid. This Mexico City scenario represents a future where cooperation, sustainability, and trust are the norm, as people from all walks of life work together to build a better world.

(603 characters)
